stem: In a circle, $m(\text{arc } AB) = 100^\circ$. Find the measure of the inscribed angle $\angle ACB$ that includes arc $AB$. Drag A, B and C on the circle so that arc $AB$ is $100^\circ$ and the inscribed angle shows its measure. Then move C around: what do you notice about $\angle ACB$?
solution: The inscribed angles $\angle AEB$, $\angle ADB$ and $\angle ACB$ all include the same arc $AB$, which measures $100^\circ$.
An inscribed angle is half the measure of the arc it includes: $m(\angle ACB) = \frac{1}{2} m(\text{arc } AB)$.
The same holds for $\angle AEB$ and $\angle ADB$: each is $50^\circ$, so inscribed angles on the same arc are equal.

hints.text: Check what the angle at C measures compared with the arc it faces. How are an inscribed angle and its arc related?
Look at which arc the angle at C faces. C must be on the opposite side from the $100^\circ$ arc AB, so that the angle includes that arc.
Use the given arc of $100^\circ$ and the rule that an inscribed angle is half of its arc to find the angle, then set it.

notes: Part 1 (yes/no) and part 3 (explain) are not constructions. Drill-1 and drill-3 depend on figures not shown and read angles rather than construct them, so they are not templated. Proof and concyclic-judgement exercises are not constructions.
